feature: Panel sections open and shut smoothly
summary: Clicking a section header in the right hand panel now grows or shrinks the section in about a quarter of a second, uncovering its rows from the top down, while every section under it slides along on the same curve. Before, it jumped open and shut with nothing animated at all.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open any recording (File > Open Sample Recording works) and pick its clip on the timeline.

try.do: Click the TIME header in the right hand panel to shut it.
Click TIME again to open it, and watch Speed and Sound come into view from the top while Channel slides down.
Shut and open Fades, Gain and Appearance the same way.
Click one header five times as fast as you can, and check it lands settled, never half open.
Open any picture, draw a rectangle, and fold Layers, Appearance, Effects and Motion.

evaluate: Does a section start moving the moment you let go of the click, with no wait before it?
Does the motion feel like the timeline dock opening, or should it be faster or slower?
When a section shuts, do the rows under it climb up cleanly without drawing over the rows being hidden?
Does clicking quickly several times ever leave the panel looking wrong?
rough: The very first fold after the app launches still costs one long pass of about 25ms (about one and a half frames). It was the same before this change, and a second recording in the same launch pays only 7ms, so it is SwiftUI warming up once per launch. The walk reads it but does not judge it.
Motion starts about 50 to 70ms after the click as filmed, against 43ms for the old instant jump: the spring starts gently, so its first frame moves very little.
In a picture, the window filmed one gap of 26 to 34ms early in the slide where it drew no new picture. In a recording it drew a new one every 9ms through the slide.
Reduce Motion makes the fold instant in the code, but no walk turns Reduce Motion on, so that path is untested on the running app.
The mocks do not draw this motion; they only say a header collapses its group. The header itself looks the same as before.
